limitations: This is an illustrative quality-budget calculation, not a measured molecular freshness, spoilage rate, pathogen-growth or consumer-illness model.
Q10, initial equivalent age, reference life and temperature domain are chosen assumptions; AEGIS has no calibrated production poultry quality profile.
A 240-hour demonstration budget is not a recommended poultry storage life or a validated label date.
The future clock assumes the selected future product temperature persists. It is not an observed future temperature or weather forecast.
Product/packaging, initial microbial load and other quality mechanisms need product-specific validation before operational use.
Each interval uses its preceding temperature observation as an explicit piecewise-constant assumption; unobserved spikes remain possible.
Missing coverage, duplicate/out-of-order times, missing product temperature or temperatures outside the chosen model domain abstain from a remaining-life estimate.
Humidity, vibration, ambient temperature and ethylene are retained contextual channels. No unsupported poultry decay coefficients or ambient-to-core conversion are applied.
Sensitivity limits compare chosen Q10 parameters; they are not confidence intervals, guaranteed bounds or validation evidence.
Cooling does not restore consumed reference-equivalent budget. A changed future temperature assumption can change the forward clock.
This quality estimate cannot extend a manufacturer use-by date, override a hold/recall or replace a qualified food-safety/disposition review.

limitations: Rescue options are automatic calculations only. Consequential lot, inventory, assignment and dispatch changes require a separate identified human review and current-state recheck.
A projected quality clock is not a food-safety clearance. Held, recalled and ineligible lots and trucks stay blocked regardless of the estimated freshness or travel objective.
Recipient confirmation and receiving capacity are supplied planning inputs. In the AEGIS demo they describe simulated recipients, not real buyers or verified supply contracts.
Receiving capacity means NET available capacity after committed work. Distribution-center outbound capacity is not reinterpreted as spare receiving/storage capacity.

Distribution-center transfers can be shown as review-only contingencies. The current core dispatch optimizer serves existing destination nodes; these transfer rows cannot be dispatched through this recommendation.
Routing duration and geometry retain supplied provenance/fallback labels. Neither ordinary-driving OSRM nor a distance estimate establishes truck-safe eligibility or current closure avoidance.

The caller must provide the remaining quality clock at a declared future cargo temperature and any independent use-by cap. Missing sensor coverage or an unscored clock cannot become an eligible rescue.

limitations: FEFO and FIFO receive the same stock, demand, capacity, eligibility, quality-window and provided use-by constraints. FIFO is not permitted to ship held, recalled or unscored stock.
Remaining clocks must be projected hours at the declared FUTURE cargo-temperature assumption, not reference-temperature equivalent hours. The caller owns kinetic coverage and parameter provenance.
A modeled quality clock is not measured molecular freshness, a pathogen-growth estimate, food-safety clearance or authority to extend a manufacturer use-by limit.
The recommendation sequences one-wave picks; it does not create a warehouse labor timetable, reserve inventory, impose a hold or dispatch a truck.
Unselected inventory whose supplied quality clock ends within the chosen horizon is projected expiry exposure, not measured waste or an instruction to discard food.
A missing independent use-by clock is reported as missing; no actual manufacturer date is inferred from a simulated quality budget.

provenance.logistics: Simulated network; assumed warehouse placements and receiving acceptance. No actual contracts or physical vehicle location.

gateway.notice: Gateway bearer token stays server-side. Registered device/source declarations do not establish physical calibration or real lot traceability.

limitations: All logistics, receiving agreements, warehouse placement and replay sensors in this application are simulated.
Q10 coefficients and starting quality ages are illustrative assumptions, not a trained AI model, calibrated poultry shelf life or molecular freshness measurement.
A temperature-driven quality estimate cannot establish pathogen safety, extend a supplied use-by limit, or replace a food-safety disposition review.
Humidity, vibration and ethylene are contextual readings; no unsupported poultry decay coefficients are applied to them.
Routes begin at the assumed simulated origin. No physical truck position, verified buyer contract, commercial-vehicle clearance or automatic closure avoidance is established.
Replay and gateway ingestion update this experiment only. Human approval separately replaces the checked simulated distribution plan; picks do not consume an inventory ledger.
export_note: Captured experimental quality estimates and planning evidence; no certification of freshness, safety or commercial-truck eligibility.
